velocity_note: RECONCILED BEFORE QUOTING, per the PLAT-10 gate, and the three figures DISAGREE in a way that is information rather than a defect. As-scoped from docs/sprints/sprint-04.json at the moment of reading: 16 items, 64 points. Computed by the tracker: planned 69, completed 69, parked 0, moved out 0, unfinished 0, across 17 items. The difference is UI-12 (5pt), which did not exist at planning and was created mid-sprint from UI-06's own first live gate run. Moved-out is reported although it is zero, because a column that appears only when non-zero is a column nobody knows to look for. THE FULL GROWTH LEDGER, because 'as-scoped' itself moved twice: the sprint was planned at 48 points across 11 items on 31 Aug; UI-04's rendered audit added UI-07 through UI-11 (16pt, marked added_after_scoping in the file); UI-06's gate then added UI-12 (5pt). 48 -> 64 -> 69. Both growths came from evidence produced after approval and both were surfaced to the owner as they happened, which is the Sprint 02 behaviour the retro said to keep.
sizing_accuracy: Sizing held and nothing was narrowed. No item was parked, none left the sprint, and no DoD was rewritten to fit what was achieved - the one attempt to close an item short was caught and reversed (see process_findings). The sprint grew 44% (48 -> 69pt) and every added point came from a measurement, not from scope creep: UI-07..UI-11 from UI-04's rendered audit, UI-12 from UI-06's gate. TWO ITEMS WERE MIS-SIZED, both under: UI-06 at 8pt built a gate, a CI workflow, committed fixtures, a 132-case self-test AND kept extending itself as later items found new defect classes - it was the largest real effort in the sprint. UI-12 at 5pt spent most of its time on an investigation that correctly concluded in a refusal. Neither overran its DoD; both were worth more than their number.

learnings.finding: CONCURRENCY IS THE WHOLE STORY OF THIS SPRINT, and it is measurable. Sprint 03 ran 6h 56m active against 25h 39m elapsed - 73% IDLE. Sprint 04 ran 3h 51m active against 4h 08m elapsed - 7% idle, 19 agent runs, 6,808 steps, across 11 concurrent worktrees with ZERO collisions. The owner's directive ('if it can be done concurrently, always do that') is responsible for essentially all of that delta. The enabling correction was conceptual, not technical: THE CONSTRAINT IS THE CHECKOUT, NOT THE AGENT. The CEO's first plan serialised six design items into three pairs because creative-director owned two of them - which would have tripled wall-clock for nothing, since every dispatch is its own process and a persona is a file any number of sessions can load.

learnings.finding: GATES FIRED. PROSE DID NOT. AGAIN - and this sprint produced the cleanest proof yet, in both directions. FIRED: UI-06's layout gate found a defect nobody had seen on its FIRST live run (25 upscale + 31 aspect violations, filed as UI-12). UI-12's own bandwidth gate then fired and correctly built nothing. SEO-12's regression suite proved the CEO's original DoD would have killed the site's best-converting query. DID NOT FIRE: DES-03 specified a homepage 'diversity rule' as prose plus a drawing - it was never built, and the front page still shows one category thirteen times. The spec also draws a 300px desktop rail and an in-article TOC; DALAM ARTIKEL INI appears twice in the spec and ZERO times in production. The hero-eligibility rules from the SAME section, which were expressible as code, shipped exactly (UI-03's R8a/R8b/R8c).
learnings.file_changed: docs/plans/aug-30-2026-session-01/aug-31-2026-audit-spec-vs-build.md, and the finding is now the framing for Sprint 05
learnings.why: Same specification, same author, same sprint. The parts written as enforceable rules reached production; the parts written as prose and a drawing did not. That is the sharpest available evidence for the company's central finding, and it means a design spec should be read as 'which of these can fail a build' rather than 'is this a good design'.

learnings.finding: THE CEO REPORTED A CONCLUSION FROM A SUMMARY, ON THE ONE QUESTION THE OWNER ASKED. Told the owner 'DES-03 was built faithfully, the ceiling is the art direction' having read the DES-03 BRIEF and never opened the SPECIFICATION. The owner replied 'refer to the design artifacts'. The spec's section 5.3 had already measured the exact complaint - thirteen items, all thirteen from one category - before the build began. WORSE, THE SPEC IS ALSO WRONG: it points to 'the diversity rule - see H6 in section 7', and H6 does not exist. Section 7 is the state set; the four word-boundary H6 matches are three base64 fragments inside embedded font data plus the dangling reference itself.
learnings.file_changed: skillcentral/agents/projects/hellokahwin/Executive/ceo-hellokahwin.md (new section, written LAST after the team's edits)
learnings.why: The CEO wrote 'check the artefact, never a summary of it' into its own persona after Sprint 02 and broke it here. Two consequences worth keeping: a brief describes what a spec was ASKED to contain, only the spec says what it contains; and when a document points somewhere, follow the pointer before repeating the claim. The correction also CUT the work - re-opening the art direction went from 'a sprint, the owner's call' to the smallest of three tracks.

learnings.finding: THE SAME VERIFICATION SHAPE RECURRED ABOUT TWELVE TIMES IN ONE DAY, AND THE STANDING RULE CAUGHT NEARLY ALL OF IT. Every instance was 'checked a proxy with a pattern nobody tested': grep -c Kredit returning 0 on a page carrying 40 credits under an English label; an item-for-item diff showing every line changed (CRLF vs LF) TWICE; $HOME inside a loop reporting '0 json items' because of the space in 'Ian Ng'; comm on CRLF lists; an unquoted --repo-root list rejected by run-stats - the space AGAIN, third time in one day; a 5-page sample that appeared to disprove UI-05 but was drawn entirely from the affected subset; a grep for the Stage 9 heading missing three logs that used tables; and p.hk-eyebrow.truncate reporting '0 clipped' while matching ZERO elements because the fix removed that class.
learnings.why: Two would have produced a false accusation against an agent that was right. The generalisation is cheaper than the rule it replaces: do not test for what you assume is there, ENUMERATE what is there. grep -oi <pat> | sort | uniq -c answers a question about the page; grep -c <assumed-string> only ever answers a question about your own assumption.

learnings.finding: orca terminal send TYPES BUT DOES NOT SUBMIT, and a 'Sent N bytes' receipt is not delivery. The CEO sent PLAT-15 a 1,119-byte instruction to fix a failing DoD, got 'Sent 1119 bytes', re-armed the watcher and moved on. The agent sat with the text unsubmitted in its prompt, the board still read IDLE/DONE, and nothing anywhere indicated the message had not been received. Found only by re-reading the terminal and seeing the CEO's own words sitting at the prompt.
learnings.file_changed: skillcentral/skills/startsprint/SKILL.md (new section: send the newline as a separate call, then CONFIRM the state changed to WORKING)
learnings.why: IDLE/DONE after a send means the send failed, not that the agent finished - a new instance of the company's named failure shape, unknown collapsing into the value that means fine.

learnings.finding: THE CEO MANUFACTURED ITS OWN FALSE ALARM, TWICE, THROUGH WATCHER MECHANICS. (1) Arming ten watchers inside a minute made them heartbeat in unison; fifteen minutes later seven fired together, which is exactly the clustering signature the skill teaches you to read as a fleet auth event. The full auth check was run on a completely healthy fleet. Staggering the intervals 660s-1380s stopped it. (2) Every gate this company ships adds a completion-shaped string that means completion for ONE item and noise for every other: UI-06's UILINT EXIT and SEO-12's SERPSHAPE EXIT tripped watchers on UI-06, UI-09 and UI-11 mid-run while all three were still WORKING.
learnings.file_changed: skillcentral/skills/startsprint/SKILL.md (both, with the rule that ITEM EXIT is the only item-level signal) and PLAT-13's DoD in the backlog
learnings.why: The company is deliberately building more gates, so this gets worse rather than better. PLAT-13's DoD now requires real mid-run gate lines in the must-not-fire set, which is the only form of the lesson that will fire.

learnings.finding: run-stats' DOCUMENTED INVOCATION UNDER-MEASURES BY 60%. The skill names three repo roots. Sprint 04 ran in 23 trees - three checkouts plus twenty Orca worktrees. Passing the three named roots reported 1h 38m / 1,297 steps / 3 agents; passing all 23 reported 3h 51m / 6,808 steps / 19 agents. The three-root run was NOT empty, which is why it is dangerous: it looked like an answer. It was caught only because 3 agents is visibly wrong for a sprint whose dispatch map lists 19.
learnings.file_changed: skillcentral/skills/endsprint/SKILL.md (the root list is now built from what exists, with the quoting requirement and a sanity-check against the dispatch map)
learnings.why: This is the third consecutive sprint with a run-stats defect - empty in 01 and 02 (wrong key, fixed by PLAT-12), wrong scope in 04. A tool pointed at the wrong roots does not fail loudly; it succeeds at measuring the wrong thing.

learnings.finding: A SPRINT ITEM WAS SILENTLY DESTROYED BY A KEY COLLISION. Item keys are unique per SCOPE, not globally, and sprint add UPSERTS. PLAT-16 in the backlog was the creative-director name collision the CEO deferred; an agent later filed a different platform item under the same key and the original content is gone. UI-12 now means two different things - card-thumbnail geometry in Sprint 04 (done, carrying CEO evidence) and the pillar-hub item in the backlog. Recovered as PLAT-17 only because the CEO happened to re-read the backlog while answering 'what's next'.
learnings.file_changed: PLAT-17 (the recovered item) and PLAT-18 (the store defect) filed in the backlog
learnings.why: On a store whose evidence is explicitly append-only, a silent overwrite is the wrong failure mode. Nothing warned, and the loss was invisible in every view.

process_findings: WHAT HELD, and it is the thing that most needed to: THE REVIEW GATE. PLAT-15 marked itself done; verification found sprint-02.json still carrying SEO-04 as 'todo' against a tracker holding 19 items, which makes a closed sprint read as 5 points abandoned. The CEO REVERSED the done rather than accept it or narrow the DoD - and the agent, sent back, then found something far worse on its own: its first reconcile had been DESTROYING EVIDENCE, overwriting file entries wherever the tracker held fewer, losing seven records outright including three emptied entirely. It fixed the merge, added three regression tests, restored all seven and added a preservation check. Its own diagnosis is the line worth keeping: its earlier check verified ten fields byte-identical to HEAD and EXCLUDED evidence as 'tracker-owned' - an assumption, not a measurement, and the same failure the item existed to fix. NO ITEM WAS MARKED DONE ON AN AGENT'S REPORT ALONE: all 17 were verified by the CEO against live production or the artefact itself, with evidence recorded separately from the agent's claim. WHAT BROKE: the CEO's own judgement twice, in opposite directions. It HELD the RISK-09 install on a wrong model of a guard whose negative controls it had already read passing - while three writers shared the docs checkout, which is the exact hazard the guard was built for; it took SEO-12 reporting that to reverse it. And it reported a conclusion about DES-03 from the brief rather than the spec, on the one question the owner had asked. ORDERING WORKED: the CEO captured pre-fix production as committed fixtures BEFORE any fix shipped, which removed an ordering hazard that would otherwise have forced UI-06 to fabricate, revert production, or narrow its DoD to prove its gate. Two near-misses were caught by checking rather than by luck: UI-01 was dispatched into a worktree 42 commits behind master containing ZERO of the .s-row code, and the bare name creative-director resolves to a social-VIDEO persona in a fresh worktree - a video producer was one dispatch from a CSS grid bug. WHAT NEEDS FIXING NEXT: the sprint fixed defects and the owner's actual complaint was never only defects. UI-04 said so on the day - 'the genuinely broken desktop homepage, PLUS art-direction problems that apply at every width' - and the CEO reported that sentence to the owner and then acted on only the first half.
shipped_check: EVERY ITEM IS VISIBLE TO THE OWNER. Verified at close across all three checkouts and every Orca worktree, not 'both repos': hellokahwin (docs) 0 unpushed 0 dirty; hellokahwin-site 0 unpushed 0 dirty; buddy 0 unpushed 0 dirty. Three site worktrees showed commits ahead of their own branch ref (ui03-hero 7, ui08-attrib-link 10, ui11-tap-targets 18) and ALL THREE were verified by CONTENT as ancestors of origin/master - they are merge commits pulling master in, the mirror image of the squash-merge trap this company already documents. Live and checkable by the owner: the homepage at hellokahwin.com (headline column 44px -> 412px on all 12 cards, nav 9 of 9 links inside the viewport at 1280/1440/1920, hero a purpose-built 4.3:1 crop at 0.1% aspect delta and 1.00x upscale), the article pages (Kredit: as a single Malay label in one casing, attribution links 0% hidden at three widths, 67 characters per line at 1024/1440/1920), /artikel at 390px (17 category labels, 0 clipped), search (16px type, accessible name, 2px focus ring, aria-live). ONE EXCEPTION, DOCUMENTED AND ACCEPTED: UI-12 left a single image-aspect violation - one portrait cover no existing crop can fix without spending 4.2x the bytes on an 80x60 thumbnail. The agent refused and the CEO verified its costing independently. Filed as CONT-15.
